mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-9.7 to -4.9), indicating accelerating reopening momentum that will continue to push retail mobility upward over the next four weeks absent a new shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -9.7 to -4.9 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite the prior three-week uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -45 percent from baseline, it signals relaxed restrictions or increased commuter confidence, which within two weeks drives a corresponding rise in RETAIL_REC as commuting-linked shopping resumes.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -45 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -51.4 to -46.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses above -45, or declines despite the threshold being met.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects a joint return to in-person work and commuting; their combined upward trend compounds to produce a stronger rise in RETAIL_REC than either series would predict alone, because workers both commute and shop en route.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved monotonically from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over next 4 weeks is no greater than the sum of individual single-series predicted effects, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint improvement in both drivers.

mechanism_narrative: December in Victoria coincides with pre-Christmas and summer holiday shopping, a calendar effect that independently lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks regardless of other mobility trends, as households increase discretionary retail visits ahead of the holidays.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-12-15, within the pre-Christmas holiday shopping window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks leading into Christmas despite the seasonal shopping window, indicating the calendar effect is absent or offset.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility above -15 percent indicates increased outdoor and leisure activity, which within one week spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits as people combine outdoor outings with shopping or dining trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -15 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -19.9 to -14.3 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS reading above -15, or PARKS and RETAIL_REC move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects households spending less time at home, which mechanically frees time for out-of-home retail and recreation activity, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.0 to 4.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 4 weeks despite continued decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state reopening regime, GROCERY_PHARM mobility has plateaued near its ceiling (around 5-7 percent), suggesting essential-trip demand is saturated; this implies RETAIL_REC gains will decelerate over the next two weeks as the easy recovery phase ends and further growth requires discretionary spending triggers not yet present.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved narrowly between 4.3 and 7.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to grow at the same or accelerating rate despite GROCERY_PHARM plateauing, indicating no saturation effect.

mechanism_narrative: During the holiday season, simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT combines with seasonal shopping demand to produce a larger-than-additive boost to RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, as commuters and holiday shoppers jointly increase retail footfall beyond what either trend alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for two consecutive weeks during December
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-12-15 is within holiday season
fact:WORKPLACES rose from -18.9 to -14.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC gain over the next 4 weeks is not greater than the sum of independent WORKPLACES and TRANSIT effects, or RETAIL_REC falls despite both drivers improving.
